title: Spending her money on a night out with Pete Johnson
summary: He took the money, went to the Club DeLisa with Pete and his wife, and told Louella about Sheila Guys.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: So, it dawned on me. I said, 'Well, now! All this money. I gotta go git Pete Johnson.' I tol' Pete Johnson, 'Come on. Let's go to the nightclubs an' have us a ball.'
Say, 'Oh, I can't leave my wife right now 'cause she ain't feelin' too good.'
Say, 'Oh, man, she all...she ain't got nothin' but a headache. Tell her to get up, put her clothes on...goin' out.'
Say, 'Where we goin'?'
Reel 4

I say, "We goin' to do the town. Firs', we goin' over to the Club DeLisa where they have shows all night long." I said, "We goin' over there an' we gonna sport 'em up. We gonna have dinner an' ever-thing."
"Where you get lucky at? Where you get all that money from?"
I had about four...five hundred dollars in my pocket. I took outa her money. I show it to him, say, "Man, I got some dough, Daddy. I got four...five hundred dollars."
"You jus' went to the Western Union, sent your mother some money. Where'd you get the other money from?"
"My wife give it to me."
"Whhu-u-u-u-utt?"
"Yeah, she give me the money, tol' me to have a ball."
So we went out, stayed out all night long, beat my wife home 'bout a hour.
So when she come in here, "What's you been doin'?"
"Oh, I went cabaretin'."
"Ya have a good time? Who'd ya go with?"
I say, "Oh, me an' Pete Johnson an' his wife."
"Yeah?"
So I said, "I took some o' your money, an' we spent 'bout a hundred dollars of it."
says, "Well, that's all right. What else you do? Did ya see Sheila Guys?"
I said, "Yeah, we went by there and seed her."
says, "Now, you and Sheila Guys got to break that up.
Reel 4
She says she was supposed to marry you."

I said, "Oh, well, I don't know about all that." I say, "She wasn't s'posed to marry me. As matter o' fact, that ain't never come up until you brought that marriage business up." I said, "As far as that's concerned," I say, "I wouldn't marry her no way." I said, "I'm already married to you so whadda you worried about?"
She say, "I ain't worried." Say, "Well, whu' ya been up all night long. So have I. I'm," say, "I'm gonna take me a bath, an' I'm goin' t' bed. I don' know what you gonna do."
I say, "Well, I sleep in the daytime, too." I said, "I'm used to sleepin' in the daytime." I say, "Nighttime we go to sleep. I ain't used to sleepin' at night."
So we jump inta bed.
